I've been doing this for 15 years. My father did it before me. I know this land.

My 10.1 mu grows wheat then maize on the same plots — that's just how we do it here in Quzhou. Wheat goes in October after summer harvest, maize goes in June after wheat harvest. Same land, twice a year.

**Wheat:** I'll plant the improved variety everyone in the village uses — better than the old seeds my father used, gives me more yield. I rotary till before planting, same as always. I'll water three times: once before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once at heading. If I skip one, I lose yield and I can't afford that with six mouths. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and push more urea at jointing. I spray once for weeds early, once more for aphids and powdery mildew heading into May. That's what I've always done.

**Maize:** After the combine rolls through in June, I direct-seed maize — no need to till, saves me time and money. I use hybrid seed, the kind from the ag store. Everybody uses hybrid now. Summer rains help, so I irrigate maybe twice — once at jointing if it's dry, once during grain fill. I spread compound fertilizer as base and chase it with urea at jointing. One herbicide spray right after emergence, that's usually enough.

Some of my sons work in the city. I manage the farm mostly myself. I keep costs down where I can but I won't cut fertilizer — that's where yield comes from.
